content.comment_body: The AWS cloud feature has been very challenging. I had a customer who regularly uses [product_name] devices to control pumps and valves on energy projects. Everything was running fine locally, but the customer wanted remote monitoring. We suggested two options: an Ewon gateway for direct login and access to the internal web server, or using the AWS cloud service. My initial experiments with the cloud service were positive due to the speed and the ability to view data from several [product_name] devices on one screen, much like an HMI application. We deployed the AWS cloud solution but spent considerable time trying to select the right AWS instance and still aren't sure we chose correctly. The resulting bills are nearly £40 monthly for two [product_name] units recording about 50 points each. I set data to update on change, which likely increased messaging—my assumption was that this aligns with IoT practices. The customer covers the cost, but I'm unimpressed; monthly charges fluctuate depending on web page visits, making budgeting difficult. Next time, I'd enable 'update on change' only when needed, like with a temporary activation button that triggers a limited transmission period—this would help control messaging and costs. [company_name] should provide tools for estimating message volume and costs, and allow use of brokers beyond AWS. AWS could also offer tailored packages for [product_name] devices to reduce complexity, or provide device-based pricing models. As it stands, AWS seems intentionally complicated, potentially to maximize billing. In summary, the initial excitement faded due to high costs, AWS complexity, and getting [product_name] devices reliably online (and even some manual bugs). The overall practicality is low. Hoping [company_name] will improve the product with some fundamental enhancements: 64-bit number support via Modbus and pulse inputs, 32-bit and 64-bit register handling similar to other PLCs, Modbus polling with enable control for delayed sampling, built-in Min/Max logic blocks, native email support without extra modules, direct [product_name] to HMI integration so tags transfer easily and efficiently, better cloud features with more broker options, additional modules like power meters and further temperature sensors (e.g., for thermocouples), and wiring solutions to ease physical expansion within tight panel spaces. Just some thoughts.

analysis.insight_summary: Users see value in quick multi-device monitoring through AWS cloud, but are frustrated by inconsistent costs, difficult setup, limited broker choices, and unclear IoT messaging expenses. Usability issues include the need for better pricing tools, improved documentation, and more flexible cloud options. Users also wish for advanced data handling, smarter polling features, built-in email alerts, easier HMI integration, and a broader accessory lineup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the cloud features for [product_name] devices to be user-friendly, cost-transparent, and simple to configure. Desired improvements include native email alerts, support for larger data types, additional accessory compatibility, and seamless third-party HMI solutions.
